You are an automated test verdict judge. You will be given:
1. A CLI command that was run.
2. An English specification of what the command was expected to do.
3. A diff of the files that changed during the run.

Rule on each numbered rule independently, using ONLY the material in
this prompt. Do not use tools: everything relevant is included here.

For every rule return "pass", or "fail" with a one-sentence reason
grounded in the diff. A rule fails only if the material shown violates
it. Return one entry per rule, and nothing else.

## Command

```
true-bdd us create 99.1
```

## Specification

Rules 1..2 below are this run's judged clauses — the assertions no
comparison could make. Everything else about the run has already been
checked mechanically by the test suite: its exit code, its output, and
which files it created, modified or left alone. Do not re-derive those
and do not fail the run for anything outside the numbered rules.

1. the story's as_a, i_want and so_that clauses keep the meaning of the epic's — a Claude User who wants a short summary of a Google Doc on request, so as not to have to download it or copy sections of it into a separate tool just to get a quick gist
2. the acceptance criteria cover the substance of the epic's three — summarising a shared Google Doc, the error path when the document is not shared, and the partial-summary path when it is too long — in any order, with polished wording, and with extra criteria allowed

## Tolerances

Ignore in every case, and never fail a run for:
  - anything under `tmp/` — per-run scratch, excluded by design
  - `node_modules/`, `.next/`, and any other build or dependency cache
  - test-runner output: `test-results/`, `playwright-report/`, `.last-run.json`,
    coverage reports, and anything else a runner writes about a run rather
    than as part of the project
  - lockfiles (`go.sum`, `package-lock.json`) and generated type stubs
Wording, ordering, ids and formatting are free unless a rule pins them.

## File diff

### created: `docs/product/stories/99.1-document-summary-on-demand.yaml`

after:

```
story:
    id: "99.1"
    title: Document Summary On Demand
    as_a: Claude User
    i_want: Claude to give me a short summary of a Google Doc when I ask
    so_that: I do not have to download the document or copy paste large sections of it into a separate tool just to get a quick gist
    status: PLANNED
    acceptance_criteria:
        - id: AC-1
          description: When I ask Claude to summarize a shared Google Doc, I receive a paragraph-length summary in the conversation.
        - id: AC-2
          description: When I ask Claude to summarize a document I have not shared, I receive a clear message explaining I need to share it first.
        - id: AC-3
```
